# Validation

This document can be used to validate the inputs and result of the execution of the
transaction which you are signing.

## Expected Domain and Message Hashes

Validate the domain and message hashes. These values should match both the values on your
ledger and the values printed to the terminal when you run the task. The hashes assume the
pinned nonce in [config.toml](./config.toml) (staging ProxyAdminOwner 161) and move if that
nonce or the calldata changes.

> [!CAUTION]
>
> Before signing, ensure the below hashes match what is on your ledger.

> - Message Hash: `0x4455887e44e264065ac650195e4659102a14a6d490fa3b13bb8e321b6f3eac84`

Safe transaction hash: `0x934691190657161000a89de4f378714328d52b77514f3b7981838f400da03fd9`

## For Signers

Simulate the task and check the output against this file before signing.

```bash
cd src/tasks/sep/129-U22-staging-op-uni-replica-zk-v1000
just simulate-stack sep 129-U22-staging-op-uni-replica-zk-v1000
```

Check:

1. The domain and message hashes printed to the terminal match the ones at the top of this
   file.
2. In the Tenderly link printed by the simulation: paste the `0x6a761202…` hex the simulation
   prints under "Insert the following hex into the 'Raw input data' field" (the Safe
   `execTransaction`, not the task calldata) into the **Raw input data** field and simulate; the
   contracts touched must be the ones listed in [Task State Changes](#task-state-changes),
   and nothing else.
3. The decoded `upgrade` inputs show, on both chains, game 9 disabled, game 10 enabled with vkey
   `0x0073def5…1562`, a 0.2 ETH bond and `startingRespectedGameType = 10`.

### Understanding Task Calldata

The task is a single `Multicall3DelegateCall.aggregate3` from the staging ProxyAdminOwner
(selector `0x82ad56cb`) containing **3** delegatecalls, all to the v10 OPCM
`0x91C167C7AfBd0D0ACc0AA7e4525e90B5CCcb76A7` with `allowFailure = false`:

| # | Function | Selector | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `upgradeSuperchain((address,(string,bytes)[]))` | `0x86fe1c66` | devnet SuperchainConfig `0x289d2A1b1AE6E0470D8B72E53B6E3f485f251DBb`, no extra instructions |
| 2 | `upgrade((address,(bool,uint256,uint32,bytes)[],(string,bytes)[]))` | `0x8a847e2e` | op-int-0, SystemConfigProxy `0x2fB895799975C47285f950171dABaa873b158793` |
| 3 | `upgrade(...)` | `0x8a847e2e` | uni-int-0, SystemConfigProxy `0x4c10De2C774C6b5B8c512f691058FAC6dacFf728` |

Both `upgrade` calls carry identical game configs, in the fixed order 0, 1, 8, 5, 9, 10, and
the extra instruction `overrides.cfg.startingRespectedGameType = 10`:

| Game | Enabled | Bond | Args |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0, 1, 8 | no | 0 | empty |
| 5 (SUPER_PERMISSIONED) | yes | 0 | proposer `0x0595c28b885f65Ce70d65e1A1593ac77e1F2d8Ba` (unchanged from sep/128) |
| 9 (SUPER_CANNON_KONA) | no | 0 | empty |
| 10 (ZK_DISPUTE_GAME) | yes | 0.2 ETH | `abi.encode(vkey, maxChallengeDuration, maxProveDuration, challengerBond)` = `0x0073def5ff73ea4fa3adb828fa0839943e1fbf439e669779c66dcea387d71562`, 345600 (4 days), 259200 (3 days), 0.1 ETH |

The vkey is the kona-sp1 v1.0.0-rc.1 super-aggregation vkey (superchain-registry #1426).

```bash
cast calldata-decode "aggregate3((address,bool,bytes)[])" <task calldata>
cast calldata-decode "upgrade((address,(bool,uint256,uint32,bytes)[],(string,bytes)[]))" <0x8a847e2e… payload>
```

### Pre-execution checks and execution

Run after the Lagoon activation and after sep/128. Stop the proposer before executing and
restart it on the ZK game afterwards. Confirm the live nonce matches the pin in
[config.toml](./config.toml); if not, re-simulate and regenerate the hashes:

```bash
RPC=https://ethereum-sepolia-rpc.publicnode.com
cast call 0xe934Dc97E347C6aCef74364B50125bb8689c40ff "nonce()(uint256)" -r $RPC   # 161
```

```bash
cd src/tasks/sep/129-U22-staging-op-uni-replica-zk-v1000

SIGNATURES=0x... just execute
```

### Task State Changes

Only the shared dispute contracts that sep/128 deploys are written; the per-chain contracts and
the SuperchainConfig are already on v10 and are not written. The shared DisputeGameFactory and
AnchorStateRegistry addresses come from sep/128 and depend on the OPCM's deployment nonce at
that point, so read them from the portal (see the post-execution checks).

| Contract | Change |
|---|---|
| Staging ProxyAdminOwner | nonce 161 → 162 |
| Shared DisputeGameFactory | game 9 cleared (implementation, args, bond); game 10 implementation → `0x6ec6179dfeb3f2a30c24c8c0a336f3e44cbbf310` (ZKDisputeGame 2.1.0, from the OPCM's `implementations()`), args → vkey, SP1 verifier `0x27af7710890fea51698ab6d52ca534aa5753674a`, 345600, 259200, 0.1 ETH challenger bond, shared ASR, shared DelayedWETH `0xe181e5a4520d69b22d852a200c2a46e73c774b53`; init bond → 0.2 ETH |
| Shared AnchorStateRegistry | respected game type 9 → 10 |

Game 5 and the anchor root are unchanged. In-flight SUPER_CANNON_KONA games keep resolving
against their own implementation.

Accepted StandardValidator findings per chain: `OVERRIDES-L1PAOMULTISIG,SYSCON-130`.

### Post-execution checks

```bash
RPC=https://ethereum-sepolia-rpc.publicnode.com
for SC in 0x2fB895799975C47285f950171dABaa873b158793 0x4c10De2C774C6b5B8c512f691058FAC6dacFf728; do
  P=$(cast call $SC "optimismPortal()(address)" -r $RPC)
  ASR=$(cast call $P "anchorStateRegistry()(address)" -r $RPC)
  DGF=$(cast call $SC "disputeGameFactory()(address)" -r $RPC)
  cast call $ASR "respectedGameType()(uint32)" -r $RPC            # 10
  cast call $DGF "gameImpls(uint32)(address)" 9 -r $RPC           # 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
  cast call $DGF "gameImpls(uint32)(address)" 10 -r $RPC          # 0x6ec6179dfeb3f2a30c24c8c0a336f3e44cbbf310
  cast call $DGF "initBonds(uint32)(uint256)" 10 -r $RPC          # 200000000000000000
done
```
